newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on small technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on small technical rebound.

text.p: Thai stocks staged a small technical rally on Thursday despite concerns over the bearish baht outlook, brokers said.

"The market got a lift after investors bought some large capitalised banks in late afternoon. It was a pure technical rebound from a sharp decline yesterday," said Songyos Kulvichien of Securities One.
The composite SET index closed 2.72 points higher at 634.00 on 4.7 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 0.41 point to 47.68.
Brokers said investors worried about the baht decline after the currency fell to a new record low of 32.70 to the dollar onshore early on Thursday.
"Late buying of major banks, including Bangkok Bank, Thai Farmers and Siam Commercial, helped lift the index out of the negative zone," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance and Securities.
Bangkok Bank, Thai Farmers and Siam Commercial each closed up three baht at, respectively, 169, 110 and 124.
Most major sectors fell. The finance counter lost 2.86 percent but banks and communications gained 2.06 and 1.58 percent respectively.
Dhana Siam Finance declined 3.75 baht to 34.75, United Communication advanced two to 120, and Banpu lost two to 344.
Brokers said they expected the market to fall slightly on Friday due to sustained poor sentiment with most investors feeling uneasy to carry stocks over the weekend.
